title: Meetings Bridge, before the RFP · a sketch for Starbridge by Juan Pablo García
desc: How I would make Meetings Bridge land closer on the first pass and keep late stage results out by default.
h1: Find the pain in the meeting, not the RFP that follows it
lede: Your help center says a Meetings Bridge usually takes two or three rounds of tuning, that good matches can still land in the bottom half, and that procurement already underway gets in unless someone writes a negative criterion for it. This is how I would make the first pass land closer and keep late stage results out by default.
stage: From a board meeting to a signal a rep can use

flow.label: Diagram of a pipeline from public meeting recordings to ranked buying signals

edges.label: rep feedback becomes the eval set

steps.d: A three hour school board video gets split at each agenda item with its timestamps. A match then points to the two minutes that matter, and the quote links straight there.
Keywords catch exact terms like a product category. Embeddings catch the same problem said in an official's own words, which is exactly where phrase lists miss.
Both result sets get fused and reranked against the seller's problem statement, so a strong match stops hiding in the bottom half.
A model labels the buying stage in strict JSON, along with the sentence it relied on. Awarded contracts, issued RFPs and vendor pitches get dropped here, with no negative criterion to write.
The person who raised the issue is often not the one who signs. Their role gets mapped to the likely decision maker for that board or council.
An early stage signal, the exact quote, the timestamp and who to contact. Short, ranked and checked.
Each thumbs up or down goes into an eval set. Any change to phrases, prompts or the reranker gets scored on it, including recall on the matches that used to land low.
